newsitem.title: USA: Overnight rain blessing, curse for US spring wheat.
newsitem.headline: Overnight rain blessing, curse for US spring wheat.

text.p: Overnight rain of one to four inches from Montana to Minnesota was welcomed in some spring wheat areas and cursed in others, meteorologists and crop sources said.

"The western half of North Dakota and eastern Montana really got nailed with rain the past 24 hours," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather. "In general that area has been so dry most farmers would be appreciative."
However, in the Red River Valley of eastern North Dakota, one to three inches were reported where many fields were still flooded from four-inch rains last week, grain dealers said.
"There are a lot of acres underwater. It just hasn't dried up from last week," a Hunter, N.D., dealer said.

Meteorologists said one to three inches of rain was common from Montana to Minnesota, but Williston in northwest North Dakota reported 4.54 inches and Grand Forks on the eastern border, received 3.78 inches.
"That much rain falling in that short of time likely will cause flooding," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp. meteorlogist.
Early-planted spring wheat was headed in North Dakota, but grain merchandisers said it was too early to determine if the rain damaged the wheat.
In central Montana, the rain may have saved the wheat crop that had been stressed by dry weather.

"This could be a saviour for some. It could mean having a crop or not having a crop. It (rain) was really, really needed," said a Great Falls, Mont., grain dealer. "For the spring wheat and barley it was really excellent.
Scattered showers should linger over the northern Plains Wednesday, followed by dry conditions until early next week, meteorologists said.
